notes.meaning: The main point of the whole discussion is that believers have the exact High Priest they need. Earthly priests always had to stand because their daily duties were never finished. Jesus sat down at the right hand of God in heaven because His sacrifice was complete, and He now rules with all power and authority.

Jesus serves as a priest in heaven, which is the real dwelling place of God. The sacred tent built by Moses was only an earthly sketch of this true sanctuary. God Himself pitched the heavenly tent, where Jesus continually represents His people and watches over their needs.

A priest exists to present gifts and sacrifices to God for sin, so Jesus also had to have an offering to bring. Rather than offering animals, He offered His own human life on the cross. Having completed that sacrifice, He entered the presence of God in heaven to plead the merit of His offering on our behalf.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Christ continues to offer His single sacrifice in the heavenly sanctuary, and the Mass makes this one sacrifice present again as a true memorial offering.

notes.meaning: If Jesus were on earth, He could not serve as a priest at all under the Jewish law. The law of Moses required priests to come from the tribe of Levi, and Aaron's descendants were already offering the required gifts in the temple. This shows that His priesthood belongs to a different and higher realm in heaven.

The priests in Jerusalem served in a place that was only a dim copy and shadow of heavenly realities. When Moses was about to construct the tabernacle, God warned him to build everything strictly according to the pattern shown to him on Mount Sinai. Because the earthly sanctuary was designed to point to spiritual truths, it had to match God's heavenly model precisely.

Jesus has been given a priestly work that far surpasses the earthly ministry of Aaron. He is the mediator, the go-between who brings God and humanity together, in a far better covenant. This new covenant is built on greater promises of eternal life and inward spiritual transformation rather than merely earthly blessings.

If the first covenant made at Mount Sinai had been completely adequate, God would never have needed to establish a second one. The law itself was good and holy, but it was unable to produce real heart change or permanent pardon for sin. Because that system had clear limits, God made room for a better arrangement.

God pointed out the failure of the old arrangement by showing that the people did not keep it. Through the prophet Jeremiah, the Lord announced that a time was coming when He would establish a new covenant with His people. This promised covenant would accomplish the spiritual rescue that the old system could not provide.

differ.view: The houses of Israel and Judah represent the church, which unites believing Jews and Gentiles under the one new covenant of grace.
The church shares in the blessings of this single new covenant today, while a promised future revival will bring ethnic Israel into its fulfillment.
The new covenant was made specifically with national Israel and Judah, and its proper fulfillment awaits the future earthly millennium.

notes.meaning: The new agreement is completely different from the covenant God made at Mount Sinai. God lovingly led Israel out of Egypt like a tender father holding his child by the hand, but the people quickly broke their vows. Because they refused to remain faithful to His covenant, the Lord turned away from them in judgment.

Instead of chiseling commands on cold stone tablets, God promises to place His laws inside His people's minds and write them directly on their hearts. This inward change gives them the desire and power to gladly obey Him. He guarantees a close bond where He will be everything a God can be to them, and they will truly live as His people.

Under the old system, ordinary worshipers relied heavily on priests to tell them about God. In the new covenant, the Holy Spirit teaches all of God's people directly, giving them a personal and living knowledge of the Lord. From the humblest believer to the most prominent leader, every person in this family knows God personally.

Full and free forgiveness is the great foundation of the new covenant. Saying God remembers sins no more does not mean He forgets facts, but that He treats believers as though they had never sinned. Because Christ paid the penalty, God will never again bring up their guilt to punish them.

The very moment God spoke of a new covenant, He declared the first one out of date. Just as an old garment or a crumbling house shows signs of decay, an aging system cannot last much longer. This showed that the temporary ceremonies and animal sacrifices of the old covenant were about to pass away entirely.
